questions.question: The sale of car results in __________.

options.text: decrease in sale of final products

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increase in GDP**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The sale of a car is considered as the sale of a final product, which contributes positively to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

• When a car is sold, it is counted as part of the country's overall economic output.

• An increase in the sale of cars indicates higher consumer spending, which is a key component of GDP.

• Thus, the sale of a car results in an increase in GDP, reflecting economic growth and consumer confidence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**

• GDP is the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given period.

• It is a comprehensive measure of a nation's overall economic activity.

• GDP is used to gauge the health of a country's economy and to make international comparisons.

• There are three approaches to calculating GDP: the production (or output or value-added) approach, the income approach, and the expenditure approach.

• **Consumer Spending**

• Consumer spending, also known as consumption, is the amount of money spent by households in an economy on goods and services.

• It is the largest component of GDP, typically accounting for about two-thirds of total economic output.

• Higher consumer spending generally leads to higher production and economic growth.

• Factors influencing consumer spending include income levels, consumer confidence, interest rates, and inflation.

• **Economic Indicators**

• Economic indicators are statistical metrics used to measure the growth or decline of an economy.

• Some of the key economic indicators include GDP, unemployment rates, inflation, and consumer price index (CPI).

• These indicators help policymakers, economists, and investors make informed decisions.

• Positive indicators, such as an increase in GDP, suggest a healthy and growing economy.

</ul

questions.question: As of October 2022, fire altars are primarily found in which of the following Harappan cities?

• Kalibangan also provides evidence of early plowed agricultural fields, indicating advanced agricultural practices.

• **Harappan Civilization**

• The Harappan Civilization, also known as the Indus Valley Civilization, was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, dating back to around 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE.

• It was characterized by its advanced urban planning, architecture, and social organization.

• The civilization extended across present-day Pakistan and northwest India, with major cities including Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, Lothal, and Kalibangan.

• Harappan cities were well-planned with grid patterns, drainage systems, and large public buildings.

• **Fire Altars**

• Fire altars are structures that were used for ritualistic fire ceremonies.

• In the context of the Harappan Civilization, fire altars have been primarily found in Kalibangan, suggesting the practice of some form of fire worship or ritual.

• These altars were usually rectangular or square in shape and were made of mud-bricks.

• The presence of such altars indicates the significance of religious and ritualistic practices in Harappan society.

• **Mohenjo-Daro:** A major urban center of the Harappan Civilization located in Sindh, Pakistan. It is famous for its advanced urban infrastructure, including a sophisticated drainage system.

</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is the hardest mineral?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diamond**__.

__

• **Diamond** is the hardest known natural material on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness, with a rating of 10.

• Diamonds are **carbon atoms arranged in a crystal lattice structure** called diamond cubic.

• The hardness of a diamond makes it **ideal for cutting, grinding, and drilling other hard materials**.

• Diamonds have a wide range of industrial applications due to their strength and durability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Gypsum**

• Gypsum is a soft sulfate mineral composed of calcium sulfate dihydrate.

• It has a Mohs hardness of 2, making it one of the softest minerals.

• Gypsum is commonly used in construction (e.g., drywall, plaster) and in agriculture as a soil conditioner.

• **Talc**

• Talc is the softest mineral on the Mohs scale, with a hardness of 1.

• It is composed of hydrated magnesium silicate.

• Talc is widely used in cosmetics (e.g., talcum powder), as a lubricant, and as a filler in paper manufacturing.

• **Calcite**

• Calcite is a carbonate mineral and the most stable polymorph of calcium carbonate (CaCO3).

• It has a Mohs hardness of 3.

• Calcite is used in construction (e.g., cement, lime), as a soil treatment, and in various industrial processes.

</ul

questions.question: Industrial Licensing is compulsory for five industries. Which of the following is NOT one of those five industries?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Cottage Industries** are traditionally small-scale industries carried out in homes rather than in a factory setting.
 
• These industries often involve manufacturing or production of goods by hand or with minimal use of machinery.
 
• Cottage industries are typically **not subject to industrial licensing regulations** due to their small scale and domestic nature.
 
• Examples include handloom weaving, pottery, and handicrafts, which are often run by families or small groups of artisans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Licensing**

 
 
• Industrial licensing is a regulatory mechanism to control and monitor the establishment and functioning of industrial units in the country.
 
• In India, the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 mandates that certain industries require a license to operate.
 
• The primary objective is to ensure balanced regional development, environmental protection, and adherence to national security.
 
• Industries that require licensing include industrial explosives, alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, and drugs and pharmaceuticals.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Explosives**
 
 
• These include materials like dynamite and other substances used for mining, construction, and demolition.
 
• Due to their hazardous nature, strict regulations and licensing are required to manufacture, store, and transport them.
 
 
 
• **Alcohol**
 
 
• The production of alcohol, including both potable and industrial alcohol, is subject to licensing to ensure quality control and prevent misuse.
 
• Licensing also helps in regulating the distribution and sale of alcohol, ensuring adherence to legal drinking age and other regulations.
 
 
 
• **Cigarettes**
 
 
• Manufacturing cigarettes involves stringent regulations due to health concerns and the need for product standardization.

• Folk dances are an integral part of Indian culture, each region having its unique dance forms that represent its traditions and cultural heritage.
 
• These dances are usually performed during festivals, weddings, and other community gatherings, often accompanied by traditional music and instruments.
 
• Some other popular folk dances in India include Bhangra from Punjab, Garba from Gujarat, Bihu from Assam, and Lavani from Maharashtra.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT generally used in milk adulteration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saw dust**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Saw dust** is a type of fine powder or small particles of wood that are produced during activities like sawing, sanding, or milling.

• Saw dust is **not generally used** in milk adulteration because it does not dissolve in milk and can be easily detected.

• Common adulterants in milk include urea, starch, and detergent, which are used to increase the thickness and shelf life of milk.

• Using non-dissolvable substances like saw dust would make the milk appear visibly contaminated, making it impractical for adulteration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Urea:**

• Urea is a nitrogen-containing compound that is often added to milk to increase its protein content artificially.

• It can be harmful if consumed in large quantities, as it can cause kidney damage and other health issues.

• **Starch:**

• Starch is sometimes added to milk to increase its thickness and viscosity, making it appear richer and creamier.

• Excessive starch can lead to digestive problems and is an indicator of milk adulteration.

• **Detergent:**

• Detergents are added to milk to create froth and give the appearance of high-fat content.

• Consuming milk with detergent can be dangerous and lead to gastrointestinal issues and other health problems.

• **Milk Adulteration:**

• Milk adulteration is the process of adding foreign substances to milk to increase its volume or improve its appearance.

• Common adulterants include water, urea, detergent, starch, and synthetic milk.

• Adulteration is harmful and can pose significant health risks to consumers.

• Regulatory bodies and food safety authorities actively monitor and test milk samples to prevent and detect adulteration.

</ul

questions.question: The maximum duration of a test match of cricket is ________ days.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The maximum duration of a test match in cricket is traditionally **five days**.

• A test match is considered the longest format of the game and is played over a period of **five consecutive days**.

• Each day of a test match includes three sessions: morning, afternoon, and evening, with breaks for lunch and tea.

• Test matches are played with an aim to test the endurance and skill of the players over a prolonged period, making it a true test of cricketing ability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Test Cricket**

• Test cricket is the **oldest and most prestigious format of the game** of cricket.

• It is played between national representative teams that have been granted Test status by the International Cricket Council (ICC).

• The name "Test" stems from the long, grueling nature of matches, which are meant to test the teams' playing endurance and skills.

• Test matches can end in a win for either team, a draw, or a tie, making it unique from limited-overs formats where a result is always produced.

• **Match Sessions and Breaks**

• Each day of a test match is divided into three sessions with **two breaks** – a 40-minute lunch break and a 20-minute tea break.

• The play usually starts at 11 AM (local time) and ends around 6 PM, but the timings can vary based on location and conditions.

• There is a provision for a **drinks break** during each session, usually taken after the first hour of play.

• In case of interruptions like rain or bad light, the scheduled playing hours may be extended to make up for the lost time.

• **Test Match Rules**

• Each team gets two innings to bat and bowl, and the team with the higher aggregate score from their two innings wins the match.

• If the match is not completed within five days, it is declared a draw regardless of the scores.

• In test cricket, the **follow-on rule** allows the team that batted second and was behind by a significant margin to be asked to bat again immediately.

• This format allows for a more strategic and tactical approach to the game, considering factors like pitch conditions, weather, and players' form.

questions.question: Kumaradevi, a Lichchhavi princess, was married to whom among the following Gupta kings?

__
 
• Kumaradevi, a Lichchhavi princess, was married to Chandragupta I, the third ruler of the Gupta dynasty.
 
• This matrimonial alliance significantly strengthened the position and power of the Gupta dynasty.
 
• Chandragupta I ruled from approximately 320 CE to 335 CE and laid the foundation for the Gupta Empire's golden age.
 
• The marriage to Kumaradevi, and the subsequent alliance with the Lichchhavis, helped Chandragupta I to extend his influence over the Ganges River basin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta I**

• **Lichchhavi**

• **Gupta Dynasty**
 
 
• The Gupta dynasty is known as the "Golden Age" of India due to its advancements in science, mathematics, astronomy, religion, and philosophy.
 
• It was founded by Sri Gupta and reached its zenith under the rule of Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II.

questions.question: Under which Act was the Central Legislature made of two houses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act, 1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Government of India Act, 1919, also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, marked a significant step towards self-governance in India.

• It introduced a bicameral legislature at the central level, consisting of the Council of State and the Legislative Assembly.

• This Act was a milestone as it laid the foundation for a more representative form of government, thereby initiating the process of constitutional development in India.

• The Act also expanded the participation of Indians in the governance process by increasing the number of Indians in the central and provincial legislatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **The Government of India Act, 1935**

• It was the longest and most detailed Act passed by the British Parliament for India.

• The Act provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation and provincial autonomy.

• It introduced direct elections, thereby increasing the number of voters.

• It proposed a federal structure, which, however, could never come into effect.

• **The Government of India Act, 1947**

• This Act is also known as the Indian Independence Act 1947.

• It was passed by the British Parliament to grant independence to India and Pakistan on 15th August 1947.

• The Act ended British rule in India, partitioned the country, and established two independent dominions: India and Pakistan.

• It provided for the transfer of power from the British Crown to the newly independent dominions.

The correct answer is __**Dust particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dust particles are small solid particles that are found in the atmosphere.
 
• These particles can originate from various natural and anthropogenic sources such as sea salt, pollen, ash, smoke soot, and fine soil.
 
• Dust particles can affect air quality and visibility, and can have significant impacts on climate and human health.
 
• They can serve as nuclei for the condensation of water droplets, leading to cloud formation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gases**

 
 
• Gases are one of the four fundamental states of matter (the others being solid, liquid, and plasma).
 
• Examples include oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, etc.
 
• Gases have neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume and can expand to fill any container.
 
 
 
• **Water vapour**
 
 
• Water vapour is the gaseous phase of water.
 
• It is an important part of the water cycle and plays a key role in weather and climate.
 
• Water vapour is invisible and is responsible for humidity.
 
 
 
• **Meteors**
 
 
• Meteors are space debris that burn up upon entering Earth's atmosphere, creating a streak of light commonly known as a "shooting star".
 
• They are usually fragments of comets or asteroids.
 
• If a meteor survives its passage through the atmosphere and impacts the Earth's surface, it is called a meteorite.

questions.question: Sitara Devi and Lachhu Maharaj are popular for their mastery in which of the following styles of Indian dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sitara Devi** was a renowned Indian dancer of the classical Kathak style of dancing.
 
• **Lachhu Maharaj** was a celebrated Kathak dancer and choreographer known for his contributions to the dance form.
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• Kathak is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and facial expressions, and it often tells stories through dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri**

 
 
• Manipuri is one of the major Indian classical dance forms originating from the northeastern state of Manipur.
 
• It is known for its graceful and fluid movements, often inspired by the themes of Radha and Krishna.
 
• Instruments like the Pung (a type of drum) and cymbals play a significant role in the performance.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• It combines fast rhythms and fluid movements, with dramatic characterization, requiring both dance and acting skills.
 
• The dance performance usually starts with an invocation followed by nritta, nritya, and natya.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance traditions in India, originating from Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, intricate footwork, hand gestures, and facial expressions.
 
• Bharatanatyam was traditionally a temple dance for women and has been handed down as a living tradition from generation to generation by the Devadasis.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**
 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance, and it originated from the northern regions of India.
 
• The dance form traces its origins to the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• Kathak evolved during the Bhakti movement and further developed under the influence of Mughal courts where it incorporated Persian and Central Asian dance forms.
 
• Kathak is notable for its fast footwork, spins (chakkars), and the dramatic and expressive storytelling aspect of the dance.

questions.question: Who is the head of the government among the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prime Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of the government in countries that follow the Westminster system of government (such as India and the United Kingdom).
 
• The Prime Minister is the leader of the executive branch and is responsible for running the government and implementing laws.
 
• In parliamentary systems, the Prime Minister is usually the leader of the party that has the most seats in the lower house of parliament.
 
• The Prime Minister appoints members of the cabinet and is the primary representative of the government both domestically and internationally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President:**

 
 
• The President is often the head of state, with varying powers depending on the country.
 
• In some nations like India, the President has a largely ceremonial role, while in others like the United States, the President is both head of state and head of government.
 
 
 
• **Speaker:**
 
 
• The Speaker is the presiding officer of a legislative assembly.
 
• The Speaker's role is to maintain order during debates, decide who may speak, and ensure that the rules of the house are followed.
 
 
 
• **Vice President:**
 
 
• The Vice President is often the second-highest executive officer of a government.
 
• In countries like the United States, the Vice President also serves as the President of the Senate, casting a vote in the event of a tie.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of Satyashodhak Samaj, a society dedicated towards eradicating caste injustice?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotirao Govindrao Phule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jyotirao Govindrao Phule, also known as Jyotiba Phule, was an Indian social activist, thinker, anti-caste social reformer, and writer from Maharashtra.
 
• He is widely regarded as one of the most influential social reformers in Indian history, particularly for his work towards the upliftment of the marginalized castes.
 
• Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth-seekers' Society) in 1873 to focus on fighting for the rights of the lower castes and against the social injustices prevalent in society.
 
• He is also credited with efforts towards women's education and the eradication of untouchability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**

 
 
• He was an Indian nationalist, teacher, and an independence activist.
 
• Tilak was one of the first and strongest advocates of Swaraj (self-rule) and is often referred to as the "Father of Indian Unrest".
 
• He founded the Deccan Education Society to contribute towards the education of Indians.
 
 
 
• **Periyar Erode Venkata Ramasamy**
 
 
• Commonly known as Periyar, he was an Indian social activist and politician who started the Self-Respect Movement and Dravidar Kazhagam.
 
• He is known for his efforts to eradicate the caste system and for advocating women's rights.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Ayyankali**
 
 
• He was a social reformer from Kerala who worked for the advancement of the oppressed classes.
 
• Ayyankali is renowned for his efforts to provide educational opportunities and fight for the rights of the lower castes.
